posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md: Here's 'da rules... 1) Pick your favorite. 2) Post a reply here stating which submission is your favorite. If you're so inclined, include a brief description why. This last isn't required but I'm interested in knowing what floats your boat. Others probably are too. 3) If you have questions about any of the submissions, ask in the [](http://www.holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?t=3814)[thread linked through this underlined text](http://www.holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?t=3814). Any non-voting replies in this, the voting, thread will be summarily deleted. Now for the submissions, in order of their submittal. **HoloM** "**Friends forever!**" (denisjuk on glassplate BB640, preswelled with TEA, HeNe @ 45sec) It show's a cat and two mice sitting on some stones. Here's a crosseyed 3d-view: Here's a anaglyph 3d-view : (use red/cyan glasses, red on the left eye, red/blue may work, too) wmv-format movie: Download](http://4c-s.org/v-web/gallery/albums/album16/holom_cat_movie.wmv%22%3EDownload) Movie (about 500kByte) **LarryD** **Title:** Catique **Type:** Single beam Denisyuk **Materials:** 4x5 PFG-01 glass plate, dev. w/JD-2 kit. **Laser:** 10mW polarized OEM style HeNe. **Exposure:** Approx. 1 second. The object is hand molded from modeling clay which was baked, then painted with a diffuse liquid gold-leaf paint. I made the cat and the pedestal she is on myself, but the background is an old flower pot courtesy of the FTD florist. I spent some time finding a nice looking frame to complement the design, and tried to convey and "old-time" antique theme. ![Image](http://4c-s.org/v-web/gallery/albums/album20/catique.sized.jpg) ![Image](http://4c-s.org/v-web/gallery/albums/album20/catiqueclose.sized.jpg) **Tony** "Trischizophrenic cat" ![Image](http://home.comcast.net/~stampydoo/pcg05.jpg) This is a reflection H2 on PFG-01 film, developed in D-19 and JD-2 (Dichromate) bleach. This was made from a transmission H1, made on Ultimate S-R-0, developed in Ultimate chemicals. The trick here is that there was only 1 cat - it's actually a triple exposure, and each exposure got about 40% of the nominal exposure. There wasn't enough room on the H2 to show much of the third cat - it's on the right edge... Hene laser, 25-35mW (depending on warmup). **TomB** ![Image](http://members.shaw.ca/holopix/pics/cat800.jpg) Title: "The Apotheosis of Winky" - BB-640, TEA swelling, about 600 uJ exposure, 660 nm laser diode, Amber LED lighting for pic (using laserreflections LED) with Canon A95 camera, shot is unmodified except for digital camera noise reduction step. For comparison, here's a snapshot taken in sunlight. Looks rather blah compared to the LED lighting. ![Image](http://members.shaw.ca/holopix/pics/suncat.jpg) **Kris Meerlo** Untitled - Spectra Physics 125 A laser - Singlebeam hologram - Ultimate 5 by 8 inch preshiffted plate - 4 sec exposure - Halogen light ![Image](http://www.myfilestash.com/userfiles/tirex/Cat%201.JPG) **Ed Wesly** It is entitled "Tuffy II", the cutest little black cat you ever saw. The file is slightly cropped from the original scan that I got with my roll of 35mm film dropped off at the drug store. The photograph is pretty representational of the piece itself, except for the kinetic effects of the rainbows coming in through the window whirling around. Technical notes: Approximately 5" by 7" image area in an 8" by 10" frame. Backlit. Black and white transparency on Kodalith 4556, developed 1.5' in Dektol 2:1. Sandwiched with a Holographic Optical Embellishment on Agfa 8E75HD, processed in CWC2 Developer and CWPBQ Bleach. 67mm Focal Length lens glued with Norland Optical Adhesive to cover glass. Piece completed 8/8/05. ![Image](http://www.dragonseye.com/TuffyII_sm.jpg) A larger version is available at [http://www.dragonseye.com/TuffyII.jpg](http://www.dragonseye.com/TuffyII.jpg) **Dinesh Padiyar** ![Image](http://www.dragonseye.com/holography/calvin.png) It's a 4-colour "pseudo-colour" rainbow with 4 H1's: Calvin, Hobbes, the laser beam and the background. The images are on slightly different levels, but the difference is too small (about 1/4 inch) to make it worthwhile to show as a movie or in stereo. Both H1's and H2 is on Slavich VRP shot at 514. **Michael Harrison** **Title:** Flat Cats. Two dimensional cats in a three dimensional space on a two dimensional medium. **Medium:** hand-drawn cats on card stock. PFG-01 film, treated with 1.25% TEA, developed in JD-2, bleached EDTA, same for reflection copy. **Laser:** 25mW HeNe ![Image](http://www.dragonseye.com/blog/uploads/holography/flatcats6.png) [Here's a movie as well.](http://www.dragonseye.com/blog/uploads/holography/flatcats.mpg)

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
First I want to say it was/is a pleasure to see all the entries. They are all great and I can positively comment on each of them. 

I do feel we need to define the entry rules a little more clearly as the name of the contest is the PCG Contest that is, "Porcelain Cat Group" Contest. Thus I may be reprimanded here but I feel that the hologram should be a hologram of a porcelain cat. I believe that was the basis of the contest and it also sets a somewhat standard baseline. So based on my and only my (at this point) interpretation of what the contest unspoken rules are/should be I would have to say my choice is......

HoloM

Not only is it a full scene including a ground and background, I really like the lighting effect of the background.

I hope this comment does not influence others in their judging as it is just my interpretation of the contest specs.

I really wish I had light so I could enter but the good news is I get the three phase hooked back up this Saturday. It's been three months....

Michael, I too would like to anti up $10 US toward the pot. How can I send it to you?

posts.author: edelbrp
posts.content_md:
I'm going to toss my vote to Tom. It's the best example I see of keeping the cat and a depth hologram together.

I also very much like Ed, Michael, and Dinesh's. Wow, Calvin and Hobbes with a laser pointer, great idea! Looks awesome! I love the use of layering in these. Very creative!

BTW-Ed's struck me as imaginative and using the holographic element as a creative embellishment and not the center of attention. Well done combining photography skills with holography.

Not leaving anyone out, Kris has a knack for choosing simple but sophisticated models. Tony's multiple exposure technique is fascinating. You can't help but smile when Looking at HoloM's. And, LarryD's antique feel gives a great sense of mystery. If I wasn't knowledgeable about holography, seeing this on the wall would spook me.

Phil

posts.author: DJ Mathson
posts.content_md:
What a difficult quest to try to decide which one of these holograms that I like the most. So many angles.

If we would´ve had an idea competition I would definitely have won.. but I will not tell you about the idea because I might use it in the next competition. Could not participate this time.

A note. JohnFP has a point when he says that maybe everyone should have used the same basic object, i.e. a porcelain cat of some kind. But at the same time that may be a bit boring. This is a competition mainly to encourage people to make holograms and to show them to others, then it is much more fun if it is open for more creativity. But perhaps this should be decided upon before next contest so everyone knows what the rules are.

Another note. The presentation is of course of some matter when it comes to the judgement of the entries. Some take better photographs than others. This gives a bias. But that´s the name of the game. You can increase your chances by a nice presentation. A small movie, stereo shots or pictures from different angles help a lot. (Perhaps it may make it worse when you can see possible flaws.)

So now to the judgement.

First of all, all entries are beautiful. Wish I could see them live.

Comments on them:

HoloM - Friends forever!

Beautiful. Nice composition and fun with cat and mice. Makes me feel happy when I see it.

LarryD - Catique

You really managed to get that antique feeling in this hologram. Makes me think about those beautiful russian holograms of museum artefacts. Classy.

Tony - Trischizophrenic cat

Very cute. Fun idea of a cat with split personality.

TomB - The Apotheosis of Winky

The kitsch master himself. Some sort of psychedelic back to earth (or up to heaven) or something. Nice.

Kris Meerlo - Untitled

Love it. Soothing. Mysterious. I like the soft shadows on an otherwise weird (in a positive way) cat.

Ed Wesly - Tuffy II

Pure art. I would probably go extatic of fascination if I saw it live.

Dinesh Padiyar - Untitled

Love the color. Makes me think of the early days when I discoverd holography. I was as exited about holograms as Calvin seems to be in your hologram.

Michael Harrison - Flat Cats

Simple, yet deep and very interesting. Beutiful color and intriguing shadows. Artistic. Like it a lot.

So which one do I vote for? I vote for all!

No, I know I can´t do that. So I choose:

Michael´s Flat Cat

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
Thank you. Thank you. Thank you so much. You just have no idea how warming and how generous that welcome is, your love is, your affection, and I'm gratified by it. I'm sorry that we got here a little bit late and a bit short.

Earlier today, I spoke to HoloM, and I offered him and his cat our congratulations on their victory. We had a good conversation and we talked about the danger of division in our country and the need – the desperate need – for unity, for finding the common ground, coming together. Today, I hope that we can begin the healing. In Colin's forum it is vital that every vote count, and that every vote be counted. But the outcome should be decided by voters, not a protracted legal process.

I would not give up this fight if there was a chance that we would prevail. But it is now clear that even when all the provisional ballots are counted, which they will be, there won't be enough outstanding votes for us to be able to win Tonga. And therefore, we can not win this election.

My friends, it was here that we began our campaign for the PCG holocat supremacy. And all we had was hope and a vision for a better hologram. It was a privilege and a gift to spend two years traveling this country, coming to know so many of you. I wish that I could just wrap you in my arms and embrace each and every one of you individually all across this nation. I thank you from the bottom of my heart. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you.

Source:

[http://www.johnkerry.com/pressroom/spee ... _1103.html](http://www.johnkerry.com/pressroom/speeches/spc_2004_1103.html)
